title: Jesus our groom part 2
scripture_text: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God believe also in me. My Father’s house has many rooms; if that were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you? And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me that you also may be where I am. You know the way to the place where I am going.” Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going, so how can we know the way?” Jesus answered, ‘I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you really know me, you will know my Father as well. From now on, you do know him and have seen him. Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father and that will be enough for us.”Jesus answered: “Don’t you know me, Philip, even after I have been among you such a long time? Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’? Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you I do not speak on my own authority. Rather, it is the Father, living in me, who is doing his work. Believe me when I say that I am in the Father and the Father is in me; or at least believe on the evidence of the works themselves. Very truly I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing, and they will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father. And I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. You may ask me for anything in my name, and I will do it.’’
devotional:
We need to read John 14 in the context of a Jewish wedding ceremony, and as Jesus speaking as a groom. At this time there was three distinct parts to a Jewish wedding.

Consisting of two ceremonies separated by a period of time.

The first ceremony was known as the Erusin, or betrothal. Here the man would make the four ‘I will’ statements. They both would sign the KETUBAH which was a legally binding agreement, then they would share a cup of wine. The father of the groom would pay the mohar, which was originally the purchase price of the bride, and it is therefore understandable why it was paid by the father of the groom to the father of the bride. In ancient days, marriage was not an agreement between two individuals, but between two families. This ceremony would end with the groom giving gifts to the bride that would help her cope with his absence.

After the ERUSIN the groom would return to his fathers home and build an extension onto his fathers house. This may have taken a long time, and the father of the groom would decide when the room was complete and appropriate for his sons new bride. It was then and only then was the son able to go back to his bride and bring her home for the NISUIN the second ceremony, which included celebration and consummation of the marriage.

It is with this cultural context that we need to interpret what Jesus is saying to his disciples. When Jesus says ‘I go to prepare a place for you’ he was speaking and thinking like a betrothed groom.
prayer: Father thank you are looking to see in us the faithfulness of a spouse.

Study Text: John 14:1-14
“Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God believe also in me. My Father’s house has many rooms; if that were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you? And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and take you to be with me that you also may be where I am. You know the way to the place where I am going.” Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going, so how can we know the way?” Jesus answered, ‘I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. If you really know me, you will know my Father as well. From now on, you do know him and have seen him. Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father and that will be enough for us.”Jesus answered: “Don’t you know me, Philip, even after I have been among you such a long time? And I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. You may ask me for anything in my name, and I will do it.’’

We need to read John 14 in the context of a Jewish wedding ceremony, and as Jesus speaking as a groom. At this time there was three distinct parts to a Jewish wedding.

Consisting of two ceremonies separated by a period of time.

The first ceremony was known as the Erusin, or betrothal. Here the man would make the four ‘I will’ statements. They both would sign the KETUBAH which was a legally binding agreement, then they would share a cup of wine. The father of the groom would pay the mohar, which was originally the purchase price of the bride, and it is therefore understandable why it was paid by the father of the groom to the father of the bride. In ancient days, marriage was not an agreement between two individuals, but between two families. This ceremony would end with the groom giving gifts to the bride that would help her cope with his absence.

After the ERUSIN the groom would return to his fathers home and build an extension onto his fathers house. This may have taken a long time, and the father of the groom would decide when the room was complete and appropriate for his sons new bride. It was then and only then was the son able to go back to his bride and bring her home for the NISUIN the second ceremony, which included celebration and consummation of the marriage.

It is with this cultural context that we need to interpret what Jesus is saying to his disciples. When Jesus says ‘I go to prepare a place for you’ he was speaking and thinking like a betrothed groom.
